History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 42-year-old physically active woman presents with a 2-week history of mainly right-sided knee pain and clicking that begin during runs, seeking advice on diagnosis and management.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Knee pain and clicking.
- Onset: ~2 weeks ago after increasing run distance while training for a June marathon.
- Location/character: Pain felt centrally in right knee, “moves” slightly to right side; mechanical clicking on flexion–extension during abdominal exercises.
- Timing: Pain begins ~20 min (≈2.5–3 mi) into a run; sometimes severe enough to stop running; no pain at rest.
- Course/progression: Worsening with continued training. Initial mild swelling after first run resolved with ice; currently no swelling, heat, or redness.
- Exacerbating factors: Running, repetitive knee flexion/extension.
- Relieving factors: Ice application, rest.
- Associated symptoms: 
  • Single episode of tingling in right toes post-run.  
  • Occasional mild lower-leg indentation swelling after prolonged standing.  
  • Denies giving way, locking, loss of full range of motion, stair difficulty, calf pain, colour change, or sustained swelling.
- Review of systems: Denies other joint pain/swelling, back pain, abdominal pain, respiratory or GI symptoms, fever, constitutional symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Right knee contusion from ice-hockey fall (few months ago, resolved).
- Hyperopia; LASIK surgery.
- Prior severe urinary tract infection (initially thought kidney stones; ED visit).
- No chronic illnesses reported.

Past Surgical History:
- LASIK eye surgery.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN (frequency not documented).
- Naproxen (Aleve) PO PRN (dose/frequency not documented).
- Vitamin D (dose/frequency not documented).
- Melatonin (dose/frequency not documented).
- Xanax (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Exercises regularly; currently marathon training (running up to 7–8 mi); gym several times/week; plays ice hockey.
- Cannabis: smokes an occasional joint.
- Tobacco use: not documented.
- Alcohol use: not documented.
- Lives at 60 Sloane Ave, London.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination performed during video consult; patient reports full active range of motion and absence of visible swelling at time of call.

Investigations:
- None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Right knee pain/clicking, probable overuse injury vs cartilage/ligament pathology  
  - Continue regular ice therapy.  
  - Reduce running mileage; avoid runs that elicit pain requiring cessation.  
  - Prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose not documented) to be taken with food; do not combine with ibuprofen. Prescription sent to pharmacy.  
  - Refer to physiotherapy for detailed knee examination and rehabilitation program.  
  - Consider imaging (e.g., MRI) if physiotherapy suggests intra-articular pathology (e.g., meniscus, ACL).  
  - Educate on red-flag symptoms (persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, inability to move knee); seek urgent care if they occur.

Issue 2 – Intermittent right toe tingling  
  - Currently resolved; monitor for recurrence or progression; reassess if persistent or associated with sensory/motor deficit.

Issue 3 – General musculoskeletal health during marathon training  
  - Emphasize gradual mileage increase, appropriate footwear, strengthening/stretching exercises.  
  - Continue vitamin D supplementation.

General plan items:  
  - Follow-up after physiotherapist assessment or sooner if symptoms worsen or red-flags develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected: Drug allergies, full medication reconciliation, vitals, objective knee examination.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Good; minor conversational fillers, otherwise clear.
